flags: minor: A (expects shop to be rescued) is the main trap; the tickets dated past closing could be misread as hope of rescue, but nothing in the passage mentions a rescue, so C is still clearly best
R014-01.notes: Tickets dated past the closing and keeping the uncollected tickets ('Somebody might come back') both show he can't let go of the shop's work. Paragraph citations check out (the quote is in blank-line paragraph 6).

flags: minor: B is noticeably the longest choice, and its 'train to take over' idea is the only tempting distractor; a test-wise student might rule it out because of the length alone
R014-02.notes: The grandfather turns sorting into storytelling, so the Saturdays served some other purpose. The narrator 'could not have said what the point was', which fits A's vague 'some reason other than'. B and C are unsupported, and D contradicts his expertise.

R014-03.notes: The odd label and the evasive answer 'Things that don't fit' raise a question that is answered when the drawer is opened in paragraph 6. A is a surface-level distractor (the other drawers are labeled carefully), and C and D are unsupported.

flags: minor: C is a real trap because 'go through it myself' might suggest follow-up action, but the passage never says the uncollected watches still exist or that the narrator plans outreach, so C is unsupported
minor: 'treated as clutter' is a reasonable inference from the mother's 'anything in it worth keeping' and the earlier sold/thrown-out framing, but it is one step removed from the text
R014-04.notes: The narrator keeps the drawer shut, hides it from the mother and deflects her question, which protects what the drawer means to the grandfather. A and B are unsupported.

R014-05.notes: Paragraph 1 says the sign was written 'in my mother's neat capitals'. This is a one-step detail lookup, and A tempts only careless readers because the grandfather's handwriting is mentioned elsewhere.

flags: minor: the phrase 'called in' is slightly ambiguous. It can mean the shop asked customers to collect (as in calling in a loan), so B ('telephoned ahead') has some surface appeal. Context ('the watches returned') makes A best, but a choice like 'collected/redeemed' would make A airtight
R014-06.notes: The tickets were redeemed and the watches returned, so 'called in' means claimed by their owners. C is a literal-meaning distractor and D is unsupported.

R014-07.notes: His detailed explanations of who cut each gear, and when, show that he values the history and craft. The other choices have no support.

flags: minor: D's wording 'a grandchild recalling a time when the narrator was fifteen' is awkward (it mixes 'grandchild' and 'the narrator'); 'a grandchild recalling a time when he or she was fifteen' would read better
R014-08.notes: The first-person 'my grandfather' and the past-tense 'I was fifteen' show a grandchild looking back. C is ruled out by the first person, and A and B misidentify the narrator.
